Jacob of Jüterbogk, theologian and canonist, was born near Jüterbogk in 1381 and died at Erfurt in 1465. In the world he was Benedict Stolzenhagen, the child of poor parents. In 1401 he went into the Cistercian monastery of Paradies in Poland, which gave him the names Jacobus de Polonia and Jacobus de Paradiso. His abbot sent him to Krakow university, where he took doctorates in philosophy and theology and then taught theology and preached at Krakow.

A keen wish for church reform drove him, and some of his writings hit hard at Italian churchmen. Unhappy with the slack discipline of his order, he moved to the Carthusians at Erfurt in 1441. There he taught canon law at Erfurt university for many years and was chosen rector in 1456. From his Carthusian years he bears the name Jacobus Carthusianus.
